{"version": 1, "content": "

MODELS AND NODES USED IN THIS WORKFLOW

 How this works

  1. Run one of the Image to 3D Model workflows first. It writes a .glb into ComfyUI/output/3d.
  2. On the Load 3D node press upload 3d model and pick that .glb. ComfyUI copies it into input/3d so the node can see it.
  3. Drag inside the 3D view to rotate to the angle you want, then press Run.

Flux Klein redraws that angle as a finished picture. Because it is always the same 3D model, every angle you render is the same object, which is what you cannot get by asking an image model for another view.

{"version": 1, "content": "

SETTINGS FOR YOUR CARD

This workflow only redraws a picture, so there is nothing to tune for quality except the render size, which has its own note next to that node.

 What it costs

Measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090
A render at about 1 megapixel2.6 seconds
The biggest size, 1536 x 15364.5 seconds
The first run after starting ComfyUIabout 7 seconds longer
Memory in use at the busiest moment21.4 GB

That 21.4 GB is what ComfyUI chose to use when it had 24 GB free, not what the workflow needs. It spreads out when there is room and packs down when there is not, so a smaller card can still run this. It was only measured on the big card here, so treat a small card as untested rather than ruled out.

 The sampler

Four steps at a CFG of 1 with euler and simple. Those are the turbo settings this model is built for and they do not need changing. If you want slightly crisper edges, try 6 to 8 steps - it costs roughly that much more time.

 If you run out of memory

  • Lower the render size first. It is by far the biggest lever here.
  • Close other programs using the graphics card, browsers included.
  • The 3D model itself barely matters. A 50 MB textured .glb loads no slower than a 6 MB one, because only the picture of it reaches the sampler.

{"version": 1, "content": "

RENDER SIZE

Every size in the list was run on a 24 GB RTX 4090 and checked. All seven came out at the exact size asked for, with no stretching and nothing repeated. The three squares are listed first because they always keep the angle of your 3D view - see the warning at the bottom.

SizeShapeTime
1024 x 1024square2.6 s
1280 x 1280square3.5 s
1536 x 1536square4.5 s
1152 x 8964:32.6 s
1216 x 8323:22.6 s
1344 x 76816:92.6 s
1536 x 640wide2.6 s

Anything around one megapixel costs the same 2.6 seconds, so pick the shape you want rather than the smallest one. Going bigger is what costs time. The first run after starting ComfyUI adds about 7 seconds while the model loads.

Use Portrait / Landscape on the node to flip any of them, so a tall version of each is already there.

 Leave the 3D grid off

The 3D view is photographed exactly as you see it, and that picture is what the model works from. With the grid on, its lines are captured too and can turn up in the finished image. It is off in this workflow. If you switch it on to line something up, switch it back before you Run.

 Tall shapes can tilt the object

The 3D view is photographed at the size set on the Load 3D node, which is 1024 x 1024. The render size only changes the shape of the finished picture, not that photograph.

So if you pick a tall size, the model is given a square photograph and a tall frame to fill, and it is free to tilt the weapon to fill the space. Tested at 640 x 1536 on four seeds: two kept the angle and two rotated it, one of them by about sixty degrees.

Landscape and square are safe. All seven sizes were clean in landscape. If you want a tall picture and the angle matters, set the width and height on the Load 3D node to the same shape as your render size, then drag inside the 3D view once so it takes a fresh photograph at that shape. Proven in testing: once the photograph matches the frame, both of the seeds that had rotated kept the angle.

Or use 6. Keep the Angle, the other Flux Klein workflow in this set. It paints the picture on top of your 3D view instead of composing a new one, so the angle survives any shape, and the picture size comes from the Load 3D node rather than a list.
